final_interpretation_rules: The quantum strategies are compared in a common logical Toffoli-equivalent proxy inherited from EXP10 and EXP12.
The classical baseline is NOT converted into the same TE unit. Therefore EXP13 does not claim a classical-versus-quantum runtime speedup.
Inner sector amplification and outer key-marking amplitude amplification are jointly optimized.
The outer good predicate explicitly includes data=0^13, so residual non-zero-Walsh amplitude cannot be incorrectly counted as useful key signal.
If the joint optimum uses substantially fewer than 39 inner-AA iterations, then near-perfect correlation sector preparation is not globally cost-optimal.
The dominant resource should be identified from the state-preparation versus marking-oracle cost breakdown.
limitations: QROM and reversible-arithmetic costs remain analytical logical resource models rather than fault-tolerant hardware syntheses.
No surface-code, routing, magic-state factory, clock rate, or hardware error model is included.
EXP09 marking retention and conditional marked-state probabilities are statistical averages over validation subsets.
The classical and quantum resource units remain different, preventing a defensible absolute speedup claim.
